The Delhi High Court has granted bail to former Director General of Health Services Dr. Vatsala Aggarwal and former head of the Central Procurement Agency’s office Dr. Vinod Kumar Ranga in an alleged corruption case involving the procurement of medical equipment, medicines and hospital supplies for Delhi government hospitals.
In an order passed on November 6, the court observed that the Anti-Corruption Bureau’s (ACB) case was based on official records, most of which had already been seized. It said the pending investigation into the financial trail, the role of other persons and forensic reports did not justify the continued custody of the accused.
Dr. Ranga was arrested on June 18 and Dr. Aggarwal on June 27.
Opposing their bail applications, the prosecution argued that the case involved a large-scale economic offence resulting in a loss of ₹842 crore in public funds. It also alleged that the accused had yet to hand over certain files and mobile phones.
The court, however, held that the non-recovery of “missing tender files” and mobile phones did not warrant continued detention, noting that the files had remained untraced despite searches of eight premises and several months of custody.
“Pre-trial detention cannot be employed as a means of compelling an accused to produce documents which he is alleged to have made away with. It is undoubtedly a matter for trial to decide as to who removed the files and with what intent. At this stage, bail cannot be withheld as a form of pre-trial punishment,” the court said.
It further observed that both accused were doctors with permanent residences in Delhi and no criminal antecedents, and were therefore not flight risks.
The court directed them to surrender their passports, refrain from leaving Delhi-NCR or the country without permission, and cooperate with the investigation, among other bail conditions.
The ACB has alleged that Rajiv Kumar, alias Rajiv Rangeela, operated several firms in the names of other persons and, in collusion with public servants, manipulated tenders to secure supply orders for Delhi government hospitals.
One of the transactions under investigation involves the procurement of 448 portable X-ray machines. According to the prosecution, the manufacturer had quoted ₹14.92 lakh plus GST per machine, while the supplier, F-Med Devices, allegedly sold them to the government for ₹37.8 lakh each.
The trial court had rejected the bail applications of Dr. Aggarwal and Dr. Ranga on October 17.
